title: Clean toilets, healthy children and waste that stays out of the yard

say: Clean toilets, healthy children and waste that stays out of the yard.
This is the video for module 3 of Home Hygiene and Sanitation: Toilets, Children and Waste.
A toilet protects your family only when faeces stay inside it.

say: That means the bowl or slab is clean, the hole is covered, flies cannot get in and out, and nothing leaks into drains or wells.

say: Shared toilets usually fail because nobody is clearly responsible.
For example, six households in Ruth's compound share one toilet, and the soap always runs out.
At a compound meeting, she proposes that each household cleans one day a week, and they take turns on Sundays.

say: Many families believe a baby's faeces are clean. They are not. They carry the same germs as adult faeces, often more. Put them in the toilet, never the yard, a drain or the rubbish.

Wash your hands after every change

say: Empty a potty into the toilet, rinse it and clean it with soapy water.

say: Children learn by copying. For example, Grace in Jos teaches her son Tunde. First she washes her own hands slowly beside him, saying each step aloud.

Let him try while you watch
Praise straight away and specifically
Week 1: 22 of 35. Week 2: 31 of 35

say: Rubbish feeds rats and flies, and old tins hold rainwater for mosquitoes.
So sort at the source.
For example, Esther in Lagos measured a week of her family's waste: 180 litres.
By composting food waste and selling bottles and cans to a collector, only 60 litres needed collecting, a cut of two thirds.
Never heap rubbish near the house or in drains. Do not burn plastics, because the smoke is harmful to children and neighbours. Use a registered collection service.
To remember.
Keep the toilet clean and covered.
Clean from the door handle to the inside of the bowl.
Share toilet work with a rota and a kitty.
Treat child faeces as dangerous, and teach by showing and praising.
And sort your waste so less of it reaches the yard.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Clean, covered, working toilet: the first barrier
Clean from door handle to inside of the bowl
A rota and kitty keep a shared toilet clean
Child faeces into the toilet; show, do, praise
Sort waste, lidded bins, no burning plastics
